parsed.explanation: Thin dossier. The only trans-relevant facts: no trans-specific offence or enforcement exists, same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2014 (repealing a 10-year sodomy statute), the government publicly endorsed the repeal and anti-discrimination recommendations, and the head of state backed equality in 2019. No documented targeting, police misuse, facility bans, or violence. Extrapolating from structural signals (functioning rule-of-law state, no trans-specific penalties, no enforcement record, no hostile state framing), the exposure is low: residual friction from an absent protective regime — no anti-discrimination law, no gender recognition — and no documented acceptance tradition to offset the silence. The marriage ban is a resident/secondary issue that does not reach visitors. Absence of evidence is not safety, but neither are documented negatives; this sits in reduced risk, below jurisdictions with documented acceptance and working protections.
